title: Semion Mogilevich Was Born in Kyiv in 1946
description_short: The FBI lists Kyiv as Mogilevich’s birthplace and uses two birth dates: June 30 and July 5, 1946.
description_medium: The FBI lists Kyiv, Ukraine, as Semion Mogilevich’s birthplace and gives June 30 and July 5, 1946, as dates of birth used. The FBI separately describes him as wanted in connection with alleged investor fraud. The supplied sources do not explain why this biographical record belongs in a Trump-related timeline or establish a connection to Donald Trump.
description_long: FBI records list Kyiv, Ukraine, as Semion Mogilevich’s birthplace and give June 30 and July 5, 1946, as dates of birth used. In an April 2022 release, the FBI and State Department said Mogilevich was wanted in connection with an alleged investor-fraud scheme involving a public company; the FBI said thousands of investors lost more than $150 million and described indictments filed in 2002 and 2003. Those are law-enforcement allegations and charges, not findings established by the birth record. This draft narrows the frozen synopsis, which asserted June 30 as a settled date and added a career history not supported by the cited birth source. The FBI itself lists two dates, so the conflict remains visible. Neither the FBI notice nor the supplied Business Insider profile explains why Mogilevich’s birth appears in a Trump-related timeline or establishes a relationship to Donald Trump. The record remains internal until an editor documents its relevance to the timeline.

title: DOGE Access Concerns at the Energy Department Raise NNSA Questions
description_short: Reuters reported DOE access concerns about DOGE staff; DOE said they had not accessed classified information, including NNSA material.
description_medium: Reuters reported on February 7, 2025, that three DOGE members had begun working at the Department of Energy while officials worried they could access personnel files and other systems. On February 12, DOE told Reuters no DOGE employee had accessed or been granted access to classified information or facilities, including NNSA classified information. The reporting does not establish access to NNSA personnel files.
description_long:
Reuters reported on February 7, 2025, that three members of the Department of Government Efficiency had started working at the U.S. Department of Energy. Two sources told Reuters that DOE officials were concerned the staffers could gain access to personnel files, federal-grant information, and financial-management systems. Reuters also reported that one DOGE member worked in the chief information officer’s office and that all three appeared in DOE email and messaging systems. This supports a reported access concern at DOE, not a finding that DOGE had opened NNSA personnel files.

On February 12, Reuters reported that two lawmakers asked DOE whether DOGE had access to nuclear information. A department spokesperson said no DOGE employees had accessed or been granted access to classified information or facilities, including classified NNSA information. That statement addresses classified data and facilities; it does not resolve every question about possible access to unclassified DOE human-resources systems. The available reporting does not show that NNSA personnel records were accessed, that files were misused, or that any foreign-intelligence targeting occurred. The corrected entry records the access concern and the department’s denial without presenting the alleged NNSA-file access as established.

title: Kennedy Removes All 17 Members of CDC Vaccine Advisory Committee
description_short: On June 9, 2025, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. removed all 17 members of CDC’s vaccine advisory committee, ACIP.
description_medium: On June 9, 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. removed all 17 sitting members of the CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), which advises CDC on vaccine safety, efficacy, and clinical need. HHS said replacements were under consideration. Reuters reported that the move drew protest from vaccine scientists; available sources do not establish later changes in recommendations or health outcomes.
description_long:
On June 9, 2025, HHS announced that Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. had removed all 17 sitting members of the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, the CDC advisory committee that makes recommendations about vaccine safety, efficacy, and clinical need. HHS said new members were under consideration and framed the decision as an effort to restore public trust in vaccines.

Reuters reported that the entire 17-member panel was being replaced and that many vaccine scientists protested the move. HHS said the members had been appointed during the Biden administration, including 13 in 2024, and argued that without their removal the Trump administration would not have been able to choose a committee majority until 2028. These are the agency’s stated rationale and reported reaction. The sources establish the committee’s removal, but they do not show what recommendations followed or measure any resulting change in vaccine uptake, safety, or health outcomes. This entry records the personnel and advisory-structure change without treating the agency’s rationale or critics’ concerns as a proven public-health consequence.

source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Washington, DC—JUNE 9, 2025— The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) today took a bold step in restoring public trust by totally reconstituting the Advisory Committee for Immunization Practices (ACIP), an advisory committee that makes recommendations on the safety, efficacy, and clinical need of vaccines to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Under the leadership of HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., the agency removed the 17 sitting members of the ACIP committee and will replace them with new members currently under consideration.

All 17 ACIP members were appointed under former President Joe Biden's administration, including 13 in 2024, HHS said.
